_about: Regression fixture for the access-control routing surface, distilled from a real-org higher-education sandbox sweep. Every case is SYNTHETIC — generic Salesforce concepts only (Salary, Account, Payment, a System Administrator profile, a CreateApprovalProcess custom permission). No real org identifiers, no PII, no managed-package payloads. Each case pins the GROUND-TRUTH output of `classifyQuestion` (packages/mcp/src/intent-router.ts) as observed at v0.1.18 after the access-surface routing fixes (P0a/P0b metadata-count + permset-group lookaheads, reverse-direction record-type/app templates, what-permissions-profile-has, role-hierarchy-structure, passive-voice profile-migration, generalized lifecycle-process). `expect` is 'routes' when the query lands on a concrete intent, or 'unrouted-gap' when it deliberately falls through to the `unrouted` catch-all — those cases document a KNOWN grammatical-direction gap the sweep surfaced (a phrasing variant the current regexes do not yet cover). They are NOT failures to fix silently: a future router change that flips one of them to a real intent should update this fixture in the same commit, so the fixture tracks the honest routing frontier rather than an aspirational one. A harness (to be added) loads `cases`, calls `classifyQuestion(query)`, and asserts `{ intent, plane, tools, gap }` equals the recorded tuple. Values were captured by probing the built router, not guessed.

cases.query: Who can edit the Salary field?
cases.note: Canonical FLS question, active voice. Regression anchor for field_access_audit routing.

cases.query: Edit access to the Salary field — who has it?
cases.note: Permission-first, then subject. Word-order robustness: the trailing 'who ... it' still matches field-access.

cases.query: The Salary field — who can edit it?
cases.note: Component-first existential-reference form. Equivalent to the canonical route.

cases.query: What permission sets grant access to the Salary field?
cases.note: DOCUMENTED CROSS-ROUTE: 'permission sets grant access' matches the object-access grant/access template (object_access_audit), NOT field_access_audit, even though the query names a FIELD. Pinned as an intentional asymmetry to catch a future retune that shifts it back to field-access.

cases.query: Who is able to edit the Salary field?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: the 'is able to' modal is not in the field-access verb set (which anchors on 'who can (see|read|view|edit|access)'). Falls through to the unrouted catch-all. Flip to field-access when the verb set is broadened.

cases.query: Which users see the Salary field in their layouts?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: 'which users see ... in their layouts' has no field-access anchor ('who can ...'). Documents the layout-visibility-as-FLS phrasing the sweep flagged.

cases.query: Is the Salary field visible to support agents?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: yes/no 'is X visible to <principal>' form is not covered by the field-access templates.

cases.query: Can a System Administrator edit the Salary field?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: 'can a <role> edit <field>' (subject-first yes/no) is not anchored — the field-access 'who can' patterns require the interrogative 'who' up front.

cases.query: Why can't this user see the record?
cases.note: Canonical record-level access question (OWD + sharing + roles, not FLS). Regression anchor for why_cant_user_see_record.

cases.query: This user doesn't see the record — why?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: the why-cant-see patterns anchor on 'why (can't|cannot) ... see'. A fact-first phrasing with 'why?' trailing is not matched.

cases.query: What's preventing this user from seeing the record?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: 'what's preventing ... from seeing' verb phrase is a synonym for why-cant-see but is not in the pattern set.

cases.query: Record visibility: why is this user blocked?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: topic-first 'record visibility: why is X blocked' has neither the 'why cant see' anchor nor a 'record' object noun after 'see'.

cases.query: Who can see the Account object's records?
cases.note: Object-level record access (reverse of why-cant-see). Anchored on 'records', so it wins over field-access.

cases.query: Who can create read edit delete Account
cases.note: Multi-verb create-bearing CRUD question is OBJECT access (create/delete are object-level), routed to object_access_audit. Distinct from who-can-access-object (record visibility).

cases.query: What's the access model for the Account object?
cases.note: DOCUMENTED CROSS-ROUTE: abstract 'access model for the X object' currently lands on field-access via the generic '(access|permission|fls) ... object' pattern, NOT object-access. Pinned to catch a future disambiguation that moves it to who_can_access_object / object_access_audit.

cases.query: List every permission set assigned to nobody.
cases.note: Canonical hygiene question. 'assigned to nobody' matches the permission-set + nobody template.

cases.query: Which permission sets are not used by any user?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: 'not used by any user' is a negation synonym for unassigned, but the unassigned-permsets patterns require the literal tokens unassigned|unused|orphan|no one|nobody adjacent to 'permission set(s)'. 'not used' (split) is not matched.

cases.query: Show me every permission set sitting idle.
cases.note: DOCUMENTED CROSS-ROUTE: metaphor 'sitting idle' is not the unused-grants vocabulary, so the 'show me every permission set' phrasing falls to the generic schema/list intent. Pinned to catch a metaphor-aware retune.

cases.query: Give me the sharing model for the Account object.
cases.note: Canonical sharing-summary (OWD + sharing rules + role hierarchy). Regression anchor for generate_sharing_summary.

cases.query: Summarize sharing for the Account object.
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: 'summarize sharing' (verb-first) does not match the sharing-model patterns, which key on the noun phrase 'sharing model/rules/settings'.

cases.query: What's the record-visibility strategy for Account?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: 'record-visibility strategy' is domain terminology for the sharing model but shares no tokens with the sharing-model patterns.

cases.query: What's the difference between a profile and a permission set?
cases.note: Conceptual comparison of two permission-model concepts. IMPORTANT: it routes to compare-profiles (a real intent), NOT to entity-resolution ambiguity — the two nouns are distinct concepts, not competing candidate matches. Pins the boundary that this must not trigger a disambiguation prompt.

cases.query: Profile vs Permission Set — how do they differ in access control?
cases.note: DOCUMENTED CROSS-ROUTE: 'Profile vs Permission Set' matches the profile-migration 'profiles ... vs ... permission sets' template rather than compare-profiles. Still a defensible, non-ambiguous route (no entity-resolution prompt). Pinned to catch a future split between conceptual-compare and migration analysis.

cases.query: When do I use a Profile vs a Permission Set?
cases.note: Use-case differentiation. Routes to profile-migration (not entity ambiguity). Confirms conceptual questions never force a component disambiguation.

cases.query: Which permission sets grant the CreateApprovalProcess custom permission?
cases.note: DOCUMENTED CROSS-ROUTE: a named custom-permission grant question matches the field-access 'which permission sets grant ...' pattern. CustomPermission grant modeling (v0.1.15) is real, but the ROUTER sends this to field_access_audit today. Pinned so a dedicated custom-permission route (if added) updates this case.

cases.query: Can I grant custom permissions via a profile?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: capability-style 'can I grant custom permissions via a profile' has no routing template. The answer (yes, via grantedBy edges) exists in the model but no regex catches this phrasing.

cases.query: Show me effective access for a System Administrator role.
cases.note: Effective (union) access. 'effective access' matches the effective-permissions anchor. Regression pin for effective_permissions.

cases.query: CRUD audit: what objects can this role touch?
cases.note: DOCUMENTED CROSS-ROUTE: 'what objects can this role touch' matches an object-access CRUD pattern before the crud-fls-audit rule. Both are object-CRUD family; pinned to document precedence.

cases.query: Which Apex methods skip CRUD/FLS checks?
cases.note: KNOWN GAP: the crud-fls-audit Apex-enforcement patterns key on 'enforce|enforces|SECURITY_ENFORCED|stripInaccessible', not the inverse 'skip ... checks'. Documents an Apex-CRUD-discipline phrasing miss.

cases.query: How many users are inactive right now?
cases.note: Live-plane runtime query ('right now'). liveRequired route to live_inactive_users — cannot be answered offline.

cases.query: How many Accounts are there?
cases.note: Live business-data count. Not answerable from the metadata vault; routes to live_count.

cases.query: How many users are on the System Administrator profile?
cases.note: P0a fix: runtime User→Profile assignment count. The metadata-count noun list no longer steals this (negative lookahead on 'users'); it routes to the live-plane count, not a Profile-metadata count.

cases.query: Which permission set groups are assigned to nobody?
cases.note: ENGINE-ARC §4 PARTIAL FLIP (was P0b HONEST GAP). PSG assignment is now checkable live per named group: sfi.live_permset_holders (kind: permissionSetGroup) returns the true holder count — zero effectiveTotal = unassigned. Still must NOT fall through to unassigned_permission_sets (PermissionSet-only, confidently wrong); the gap note is DOWNGRADED to the partial (no single-call all-PSG sweep yet), not deleted.

cases.query: Who's assigned to which permission sets?
cases.note: UNROUTED-GAP (honest current output; was optimistically labeled NEEDS-LIVE/plane=live). The broad org-wide 'who is assigned to WHICH permission sets' membership sweep has NO single-call routing template in R5 — the router returns intent=unrouted, plane=unknown, gap=unrouted. Relabeled to the router's real output rather than asserting a live-route capability that was never built (routing-grader-triage: do not hide a genuine gap, and do not assert an unbuilt capability). The building blocks exist per named target — sfi.live_permset_holders ('who holds this permission set') and sfi.live_user_permsets ('which permission sets does this user have') — so a future membership-sweep intent could flip this back to needs-live/plane=live. Until that template is built this stays an honest unrouted gap. TRAP: 'who assigned this permission set as of last quarter' stays an honest gap (historical assignment log not exposed).

cases.query: Who is in the Support Tier 1 public group?
cases.note: NEEDS-LIVE: public-group membership is runtime record data. R5 engine now routes this to the live plane via the queue-group-member-roster intent (a correct same-domain pick) — sfi.live_group_members answers group membership questions directly. Gold intent relabeled from 'unrouted' to the router's real finer output per routing-grader-triage (stale gold LABEL, router made a correct pick = TEST bug, relabel additively). TRAP: 'who was in this group last quarter' (historical) stays an honest gap.

cases.query: Which inactive users still have active licenses?
cases.note: NEEDS-LIVE: inactive-user + active-license cross is runtime query data. R5 engine now routes this to the live plane via the inactive-users intent (a correct same-domain pick) — sfi.live_zombie_accounts / sfi.live_inactive_users answer this directly. Gold intent relabeled from 'unrouted' to the router's real finer output per routing-grader-triage (stale gold LABEL, router made a correct pick = TEST bug, relabel additively). TRAP: 'who deactivated these users' (audit trail) stays an honest gap.

cases.query: What's the MFA policy for this org?
cases.note: HONEST GAP: org-wide MFA / session policy (SessionSettings) is not in the retrieve manifest today, so no route exists. The router correctly returns unrouted with plane:unknown — it must NOT claim an sfi.live_* workaround. When a SessionSettings tier ships, add a route and update this case.

cases.query: Are password policies enforced?
cases.note: HONEST GAP: password-policy enforcement is an org-wide security setting not modeled in the vault. Correctly unrouted; must not be papered over with general Salesforce knowledge or a fabricated live tool.

cases.query: Which IP ranges can log in?
cases.note: ROUTED (eval family C): per-PROFILE loginIpRanges are extracted and surfaced via sfi.profile_security, so 'which IP ranges can log in' now routes to the profile-security intent — list_components(type Profile) enumerates, then profile_security per profile reads the login IP ranges (the org-wide answer is the union over profiles). Previously pinned unrouted only because no rule existed.
